findings.heading: From SAS / Descriptive analysis table
findings.proposition: The translation attributes summary() to the skimr package; the English attributes only skim() to skimr and treats summary() as separate.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader concludes summary() requires installing and loading skimr, and may install a package to run a base R function, or fail to call summary() when skimr is absent.

findings.heading: From Excel / Benefits
findings.proposition: The English says Excel workflows rely on the user's own memory of the steps; the translation says they depend on メモリ (computer memory).
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader takes the stated source of Excel error risk to be machine memory rather than the analyst having to remember manual steps, and so misses the argument that scripted, written-down steps remove that risk.

findings.heading: From Excel / R-Excel interaction
findings.proposition: The English lists 'sideways text' as an Excel formatting feature lost in translation; the translation lists 補足のためのテキスト ('text for supplementary notes') instead.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader gets the wrong example of what R loses, and may expect rotated/vertical cell text to survive a round trip while expecting annotation text to be dropped.

findings.heading: Transition to R (introduction)
findings.proposition: The English says R has grown dramatically in scope (capability); the translation says R has dramatically expanded its user base (利用者を飛躍的に拡大).
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader receives an adoption statistic claim that the handbook does not make and does not support, instead of the capability claim that motivates the following sentence about commercial competitors reacting to R's development.

findings.heading: From Stata / Working directory table
findings.proposition: The English states that getwd() and here() are called with empty parentheses; the translation omits that instruction.
findings.reader_consequence: A Stata user reading the Japanese table does not learn that these two functions take no argument, and may try to pass a folder path to getwd() or here() by analogy with Stata's pwd usage.

findings.heading: From SAS / Working directory table
findings.proposition: The English states that getwd() and here() are called with empty parentheses; the translation omits that instruction.
findings.reader_consequence: A SAS user reading the Japanese table does not learn that these two functions take no argument, and may try to pass a path to getwd() or here() by analogy with the SAS %sysfunc(getoption(work)) syntax.

findings.heading: From SAS / Basic data manipulation table
findings.proposition: The translation of the SAS factor-labelling row says column names are not labelled in R 「Stata のように」 (as they are in Stata); the English SAS row makes no reference to Stata.
findings.reader_consequence: A SAS user reading only the SAS section is pointed at Stata behaviour that is irrelevant to their comparison, and may infer that SAS and Stata label column names the same way.
